decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark … paste a link”; Round 1 client did not contest URL-based saving.
decisions.note: Conforming baseline-specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “open a bookmark in the browser”; Round 1 client did not contest this behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming baseline-specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “optionally a title/tags” and “group by tags and filter”; Round 1 client retained tagging and filtering while requesting additions.
decisions.note: Tag assignment and tag filtering conform at the baseline-specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “delete with confirmation”; Round 1 client did not reject permanent deletion, but separately requested archiving.
decisions.note: Conforming delete decision; archive requirements are classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “No rich metadata (thumbnails, favicons, previews) beyond a basic derived title.” Round 1 client: “Saving a link should automatically collect its title, description, favicon, and preview image” and “yes to favicons and previews.”
decisions.note: At the baseline specification gate, the client explicitly rejected the stated metadata exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limited editing to “edit titles/tags” and described an optional title at entry. Round 1 client supplied the expected fields: “edit the address, title, description, tags, and a note.”
decisions.note: The presented edit scope omitted required fields and did not provide the required before/after handling of collected title and description.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented only “duplicate detection.” Round 1 client specified: “Saving an address that already exists should take me to the existing bookmark to edit it, not merely reject it as a duplicate.”
decisions.note: Baseline duplicate handling did not commit to converging on the existing bookmark; the client supplied the reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker said a bookmark is merely “shown in a list” and excluded rich metadata. Round 1 client required the list to show “title, description, tags, and favicon.”
decisions.note: The baseline list presentation omitted the readability fields required per item.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented tagging/filtering without tag-entry suggestions. Round 1 client: “Tag entry should suggest tags I already use.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing autocomplete requirement at the baseline specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “search across title/address/tags.” Round 1 client required case-insensitive search over “title, description, note, and address,” plus “#tag,” exact phrases, and “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: The presented search fields and grammar were materially narrower than the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s exhaustive baseline slices omitted read state. Round 1 client requested “a read-later state, a separate unread view, and a way to mark items read.”
decisions.note: The client added the omitted unread/read-later feature group.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s baseline scope omitted bulk operations. Round 1 client requested selecting several bookmarks or “everything matching my current search or filter” for tag, read-state, archive, and delete actions.
decisions.note: The client added both selected-item and whole-filtered-collection bulk behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s baseline scope omitted sorting. Round 1 client: “I need sorting, including by date added and title.”
decisions.note: Missing list-sorting requirement added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered deletion but no archive behavior. Round 1 client required reversible archiving, distinction from permanent deletion, exclusion from normal results, and a separate archive view.
decisions.note: The client added the omitted archive lifecycle and visibility rules.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s baseline scope omitted saved filters. Round 1 client requested “saved combinations of searches and included or excluded tags that I can revisit.”
decisions.note: The client added bundles/saved-filter behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s editing scope omitted formatted notes. Round 1 client requested a note field and said, “Notes should support basic formatting and display properly.”
decisions.note: The client added authored and rendered formatted notes; the exact Markdown choice was refined later.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s baseline scope omitted preservation. Round 1 client requested “a preserved copy,” preserving the original PDF when applicable, and “an option to preserve it through the Internet Archive.”
decisions.note: The client added both local and Internet Archive preservation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly assumed “No import/export.” Round 1 client said import and export in browser-bookmark HTML “are must-haves” and reiterated “yes to import/export.”
decisions.note: The client rejected the explicit import/export exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s baseline scope omitted settings. Round 1 client requested default sorting, number of items shown, and text-size preferences.
decisions.note: The client added display-related personal settings.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “On save, fetches title, description, favicon, preview image”; Round 2 client did not contest metadata collection.
decisions.note: Conforming revised-specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker listed editable “Address, title, description, tags, note”; Round 2 client only clarified when collected fields must be editable.
decisions.note: The set of editable bookmark fields conforms; initial-save timing is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Saving an existing address opens it for editing, no duplicate”; Round 2 client did not contest this behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-to-edit decision in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Each row shows title, description, tags, favicon”; Round 2 client did not contest the list contents.
decisions.note: Conforming revised-specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Suggests already-used tags while typing”; Round 2 client did not contest this behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming tag-autocomplete decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified case-insensitive search over title/description/note/address with “#tag” and “exact phrases”; Round 2 client retained these features while correcting two combination rules.
decisions.note: The primary search fields, case handling, tag syntax, and exact-phrase behavior conform; combination semantics are separate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker said collected metadata was editable but did not make pre-save adjustment explicit. Round 2 client: “adjust the automatically collected title and description before the initial save, as well as later.”
decisions.note: At the revised-specification gate, the client added the missing pre-save timing requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker listed tag and boolean search syntax without their interaction or quoted-operator rule. Round 2 client required ordinary text and “#tag” to both match and quoted words such as “AND” to be literals.
decisions.note: The client corrected incomplete advanced-search semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Read/unread marking + separate unread view”; Round 2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: Conforming read-later decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified selecting several bookmarks and applying add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, and delete actions; Round 2 client only corrected select-all scope.
decisions.note: Selected-item bulk actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker described “all-matching-search.” Round 2 client required the complete current view, including search, tag filters, and unread/archive perspective, “not merely the visible page.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the scope of whole-collection bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: sorting “By date added and title, both directions”; Round 2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: Conforming sorting decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified reversible archive, exclusion from normal lists/searches, its own view, and distinct confirmed deletion; Round 2 client did not contest these behaviors.
decisions.note: Conforming archive-versus-delete decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Named query + included/excluded tags, revisitable”; Round 2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: Conforming bundle/saved-filter decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker defined “Basic rich-text” notes. Round 2 client: “Notes should use Markdown for formatting, rather than a rich-text editor.”
decisions.note: The proposed note-authoring model contradicted the reference and was corrected.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker promised a “Viewable saved copy” and original PDFs but did not specify single-file local HTML. Round 2 client required “a self-contained local HTML file” and the original PDF for PDF addresses.
decisions.note: The local snapshot representation was insufficiently specified and was corrected.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker included an “optional Internet Archive snapshot”; Round 2 client did not contest that option.
decisions.note: Conforming Internet Archive preservation decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified Netscape/browser HTML import/export with titles, tags, and dates preserved; Round 2 client confirmed: “The browser bookmark HTML assumption is right.”
decisions.note: Conforming import/export decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified persisted default sort, items per page, and text size; Round 2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: Conforming preferences decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “notes are authored/stored as Markdown source … and rendered as formatted text”; Round 3 client: “those corrections capture what I want.”
decisions.note: Conforming revised decision at the final specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: fetched title and description are editable “before the first save, as well as editable later”; Round 3 client approved the correction.
decisions.note: Conforming revised decision at the final specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: web pages are preserved as “a single offline-openable HTML file with assets inlined”; PDFs preserve the original PDF. Round 3 client approved.
decisions.note: Conforming revised preservation decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: text plus “#tag” must both match and a quoted operator such as “AND” is literal; Round 3 client approved.
decisions.note: Conforming revised search-semantics decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: select-all covers active search, included/excluded tags, and unread/archive view, not only the visible page; Round 3 client approved.
decisions.note: Conforming revised whole-filter bulk-action decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presented an 86-task breakdown spanning all 13 approved user stories, from save/metadata through preferences. Round 5 client: “The task breakdown covers the approved behavior.”
decisions.note: The complete task-breakdown coverage conformed before the separate implementation-scope choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker offered “full build, or MVP-first (stop after US1 to validate)” and recommended an MVP consisting only of setup, foundations, and US1. Round 5 client selected the conforming alternative: “proceed with the full build through all 13 stories … don’t stop after the US1 MVP.”
decisions.note: Implementation-scope selection at the final pre-code gate; the offered MVP-only alternative would omit most reference functionality.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker reported delivered save/metadata, pre-save adjustment, duplicate-to-edit, full editing, and rendered Markdown notes. Round 6 client said the delivered behavior covered what was approved.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review presentation; this classifies the presented behavior, not independent execution coverage.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker reported browse/sort/open, advanced search with all specified semantics, and tags with suggestions and filters. Round 6 client accepted the delivered behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming browse/search/tag implementation-review presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker reported read-later/unread view, bulk actions by IDs or the whole matching view, reversible archive, and confirmed permanent deletion. Round 6 client accepted the delivered behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming state, bulk-action, archive, and delete implementation-review presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker reported saved searches, self-contained HTML/original-PDF/Internet-Archive preservation, browser-HTML import/export, and display preferences. Round 6 client accepted the completed application and said external preservation checks were sufficient.
decisions.note: Conforming extended-feature implementation-review presentation. Test grouping, serialized execution, and external-test strategy are orthogonal to the reference and are not classified as divergences.
